newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's former rulers in talks with ANC rebel.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's former rulers in talks with ANC rebel.

text.p: South Africa's former white rulers said on Thursday party leaders probing the formation of a new multiracial opposition alliance held talks with ousted black African National Congress parlimentarian Bantu Holomisa.

The National Party, giving little away, said it would hold further talks with Holomisa, who was campaigning to found his own opposition party by June under the banner of the National Consultative Forum.
"It is in line with the National Party's vision and mission of consulting in order to obtain a realignment of the South African political scene," the party said in a statement.
Holomisa, a hugely popular former protege of President Nelson Mandela, fell from favour last year after making public bribery allegations against a colleague and then refused to apologise.
He was expelled from the ANC last August and sacked as deputy minister of environmental affairs and tourism by Mandela.
Holomisa, 41, agreed in February to oversee the birth of a new party widely seen as a possible haven for defectors from the ANC ahead of the next general elections, scheduled for 1999.

The National Party of former president F.W. de Klerk walked out of Mandela's government of national unity last year saying they were being ignored, and is trying to widen its narrow base of white and coloured, or mixed-race, voters.
